global_organization_chain: The summary starts from geographic language shift and an office decision, then previews worldwide, domestic, geographic, fitting, forecast, sensitivity, and recommendation stages in dependency order.
The introduction separates temporal speaker forecasting, country distribution, and office choice before attributing the bilingual competition mechanism that will be extended.
Problem analysis turns policy, tourism, trade, technology, and media from a qualitative inventory into status or resistance interfaces before the governing equations appear.
Model construction moves from worldwide multi-language balance to domestic adaptation, route migration, and a single country-language geographic recurrence.
The fitting algorithm aligns observed and predicted annual changes, then hands fitted parameters to fifty-year worldwide and geographic simulations.
Results progress from quantities to shares and ranks, then from country-language arrays to ANOVA, English maps, and the marginal employee-language decision.
The office table is followed by an explicit missing-company-data boundary, three sensitivity families, source-acknowledged weaknesses, future work, and a conclusion that reassembles the chain.
The final pass records raster, definition, unit, interval, aggregation, statistical, and decision warnings without replacing positive language, organization, model, equation, or visual evidence.

main_argument_chains.claim: Worldwide language forecasting is built by extending a cited bilingual transition mechanism only after the retained and missing mechanisms are made explicit.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Reuse the worldwide forecast only with its speaker-stock semantics, proxy ledger, probability bounds, and unreadable formula parts made explicit.

main_argument_chains.claim: Geographic language change is modeled as domestic competition plus natural population growth and country-to-country migration, not as one undifferentiated effect.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Treat country forecasts as conditional until migration timing, simultaneous updates, conservation, and global-to-local aggregation reconcile.

main_argument_chains.claim: The fifty-year forecast depends on a short calibration window and a high-dimensional fitted interface whose reproducibility is incomplete.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Do not treat 2068 ranks or shares as externally validated until the parameter ledger, residuals, held-out design, and uncertainty are published.

main_argument_chains.claim: The office recommendation is a downstream marginal decision that consumes country-language forecasts and an external city hierarchy.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Keep the six-city result illustrative until city economics, employee counts, existing offices, budget, and forecast uncertainty enter the decision model.

main_argument_chains.claim: The paper's sensitivity evidence supports only local statements about the tested capacity, one-country disruptions, and Australia parameter directions.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Run joint, structural, horizon, and decision-level uncertainty before calling the forecast or office portfolio robust.

warnings.warning: Equation 11 is rasterized; tourism, trade, media, time trend, and reference resistance are visible dependencies, but exact operators, signs, scaling, and coefficients cannot be recovered reliably and are retained as f_11.
Equation 12 is transcribed at medium confidence as official-language support times a status scale plus a baseline; the raster and missing parameter ledger prevent stronger glyph and scale claims.
Equation 15 is rasterized; its country tourism, trade-to-GDP, media, time, and reference-resistance inputs are retained, but unresolved operators remain explicitly represented by f_15.
Equation 16 is retained at medium confidence as the domestic official-language indicator scaled into status plus a baseline; exact glyph and coefficient evidence is incomplete.

Equation 20 substitutes historical tourism and trade means into domestic resistance, but its rasterized combination cannot be normalized beyond the confirmed f_20 dependency interface without inventing operators.

Equation 21 divides every migration interval by five years although the stated 1991-2017 series includes a final interval that may not be five years; route timing, signs, and averaging weights require source-table reconciliation.

Equation 27 combines domestic shift, demographic growth, and migration, but global and country-language speaker stocks may overlap and are fitted at different aggregation levels; conservation and cross-level reconciliation are unproved.

Equation 29 mixes a language-covered population share, a benefit factor F, and per-language cost C; the paper's illustrative C=F=10 percent does not establish compatible currency units or city-specific economics.

request_body_guard.transport_finding: HTTP 413 is an nginx ingress rejection before model processing. The exact server limit is not observable here, but accumulated conversation history plus one-or-more base64 image bodies is the supported failure mechanism: base64 expands binary bytes and the entire request is measured together. Q125 therefore uses <=450000-byte JPEG proxies, at most one image per tool call, no full JSONL/base64 output, and text/hash checks after eight proxies.
